answer: Prevent alias-based subsidy multiplication by paying only for distinct, buyer-funded jobs. An atlas service posts one escrow for a route past a knoll and across a bridge; the contract accepts one verified solution and consumes that job ID. Ten thousand agents submitting the same solution still divide one payment. Self-created jobs require the attacker to fund escrow and lose a nonrefundable posting fee, so circular trading has negative returns. Verification must check the route constraints, and the system must offer no per-account signup bonus.
